zh: 行馆设在天后宫，上海道邵友濂率领松江知府及所属各县『庭参』，接着是江海关税务司及工部局的董事拜会，在上海的文武官员谒见，然后是邵友濂联合在上海有差使的道员，包括胡雪岩、盛宣怀在内，『恭宴爵相』，散席时，已经起更了。胡雪岩与古应春当然留在最后，『大人今天很累了。』胡雪岩说∶『请早早安置，明天再来请安。』『不、不！』左宗棠摇着手说∶『我明天看了制造局，后天就回江宁了。有好些事情跟你谈谈，不忙走。』胡雪岩原是门面话，既然左宗堂精神很好，愿意留他相谈，自是求之不得，答应一声，坐了下来。
en: Zuo’s temporary headquarters were at Tianhou Temple. Shao Youlian, the Shanghai intendant, led the prefect of Songjiang and the subordinate county magistrates in paying formal respects. Next came the commissioner of the Jiang Customs and directors of the municipal councils, followed by the civil and military officials stationed in Shanghai. Shao then joined the intendants holding appointments there, including Hu Xueyan and Sheng Xuanhuai, in a banquet honoring the marquis and grand secretary. By the time it ended, the first night watch had begun. Hu and Gu naturally stayed until last. “Your Excellency has had a tiring day,” Hu said. “Please retire early. We shall return tomorrow to pay our respects.” “No, no!” Zuo waved a hand. “I inspect the arsenal tomorrow and return to Jiangning the day after. There are many things I must discuss with you. Do not hurry away.” Hu had offered only the customary polite words. Since Zuo was in good spirits and wished him to stay, he could ask for nothing better. He assented and sat down.

zh: 『陆防、海防争了半天，临到头来，还是由我来办，真是造化弄人。』说罢，左宗棠仰空大笑，声震屋瓦。这一笑只有胡雪岩明白，是笑李鸿章。原来同治十一年五月，俄国见新疆回乱，有机可乘，出兵伊犁；十三年三月，日本借口琉球难民事件，派军入侵台湾，一时陆防、海防相继告警，因而出现了陆防与海防孰重的争论；相争两方的主角，正就是左宗棠与李鸿章。左宗棠经营西北，李鸿章指挥北洋，各有所司，亦各有所持，朝迁认为兹事体大，命各省督抚，各抒所见。其时湖南巡抚王文韶，正好回杭州扫墓，胡雪岩便问他∶『赞成陆防，还是海防？』
en: “After all that argument over land defense and maritime defense, in the end I have to attend to it myself. What tricks fortune plays!” Zuo threw back his head and laughed so loudly that the roof seemed to shake. Only Hu understood that the laughter was directed at Li Hongzhang. In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Tongzhi, Russia had taken advantage of the Muslim rebellion in Xinjiang to send troops into Ili. In the third month of the thirteenth year, Japan used the incident involving shipwrecked Ryukyuans as a pretext to invade Taiwan. Threats on land and at sea followed one another, provoking debate over which kind of defense should take priority. Its principal opponents were Zuo and Li. Zuo managed affairs in the northwest, Li commanded Beiyang; each had his own responsibilities and convictions. Considering the issue of great importance, the court ordered governors-general and governors throughout the provinces to state their views. Wang Wenshao, then Governor of Hunan, happened to be back in Hangzhou to visit his ancestral graves. Hu asked him whether he favored land or maritime defense.

zh: 王文韶反问一句∶『你看呢？』『你当湖南巡抚，自然应该帮湖南人讲话。』『不错。为政不得罪巨室。』王文韶说∶『我为这件事，一直踌躇不决，现在听老兄一句话，算是定了主意。李大先生的交情，暂时要搁一搁了。』原来王文韶跟李鸿章的关系很深，为了在湖南做官顺利，王文韶决定赞成陆防，复奏说道∶『江海两防，亟宜筹备，然海疆之患，不能无因而至，其关键则在西陲军务，俄人据我伊犁，强有久假不归之势，我师迟一日，则俄人进一日，事机之急，莫此为甚。』就因为这个奏折，使得陆防论占了上风。不久同治驾崩，争端暂息。光绪元年，争议复起，慈禧太后命亲郡王、大学士、六部九卿，会议海防事宜。李鸿章上折请罢西征；左宗棠当然反对，最后是由于文祥的支持，派左宗棠以钦差大臣督办新疆军务，显然的，海防论又落了下风。
en: “What do you think?” Wang countered. “As Governor of Hunan, you should naturally speak for a Hunan man.” “Quite. A man governing a province must not offend its powerful families. I have been unable to decide this matter. Your words have settled it. My friendship with Lord Li must be put aside for the moment.” Wang’s ties with Li were deep, but for the sake of governing Hunan smoothly, he decided to support land defense. In his memorial he wrote: “Defenses on both river and sea urgently require preparation. Yet a threat to the coast cannot arise without a cause; the crucial matter lies in the military situation on our western frontier. The Russians occupy our Ili and show every sign of holding it indefinitely. Each day our troops delay gives them another day’s advance. Nothing could be more urgent.” This memorial gave the land-defense argument the advantage. Soon afterward the Tongzhi Emperor died, and the dispute subsided temporarily. It revived in the first year of Guangxu, when Empress Dowager Cixi ordered princes, grand secretaries, and the heads of the Six Ministries and Nine Courts to confer on maritime defense. Li memorialized for an end to the western expedition; Zuo naturally opposed him. Finally, with Wenxiang’s support, Zuo was appointed imperial commissioner to direct military affairs in Xinjiang. Plainly, the maritime-defense argument had again lost ground.

zh: 不过陆防之议，实际上是由伊犁事件而来，及至曾纪泽使俄，解决了中俄纠纷，陆防论就不再有人提起。到得左宗常西征收功，内召入军机；不久又外放两江，李鸿章旧事重提，这回大获全胜，海防的计划，朝廷完全同意，首先要办的是三件事∶一是在营口设营，编练新工海军；二是筹款续造『钢面铁甲』兵轮，招商局原应归还的官款暂缓归还，拨作购铁甲船之用；三是南北洋各紧要海口修船坞、修炮台，同时并举。哪知正在干得如火如茶之时，李太夫人病殁汉口，李鸿章丁忧回籍，调两广总督张树声署理直督，筹设海防一事，便暂时拦下来了。
en: In practice, however, the case for land defense had arisen from the Ili affair. After Zeng Jize’s mission to Russia settled the Sino-Russian dispute, it ceased to be raised. When Zuo completed his western campaign, he was summoned to the Grand Council, then soon appointed Governor-General of Liangjiang. Li revived the old question and this time won a complete victory. The court accepted his maritime-defense plan in full. Three measures were to come first: establishing a base at Yingkou to train a new naval force; raising funds to continue building steel-armored warships, with government loans due for repayment by China Merchants temporarily retained and diverted to the purchase of ironclads; and simultaneously building docks and forts at the important harbors of both Nanyang and Beiyang. Just as the work gathered momentum, Old Madam Li died in Hankou. Li Hongzhang returned home to observe mourning, and Zhang Shusheng, Governor-General of Liangguang, was transferred to act in Zhili. The coastal-defense preparations temporarily came to a halt.

zh: 『海防，北洋可管，南洋又何尝不可管；而且经费大部分出在两江，南洋来管，更觉名正言顺。我现在想先从船坞、炮台这两件事着手。已经派人去邀彭宫保了；我要赶回江宁，就因为他从长江上游巡阅下来，日内可到江宁，客临主不在，未免失礼。』左宗棠一口气说到这里，突然叫一声∶『雪岩！』『大人有什么吩咐？』『福克在不在上海？』『在。』胡雪岩答说∶『他本来要回国了，因为听说大人巡视上海，特为迟一班轮船走。明天一定会来见大人。』『喔，他回德国以后，还来不来？』『来，来。』『那好。正好趁他回国之便，我们再商量商量，看有什么新出的利器，托他采办。』
en: “If Beiyang can manage maritime defense, why should Nanyang not do so? Most of the money comes from Liangjiang anyway, making it still more proper for Nanyang to take charge. I mean to begin with docks and forts. I have already sent for Lord Peng. The reason I must hurry back to Jiangning is that he is coming down the Yangtze on an inspection and should arrive within days. It would hardly be courteous for the host to be absent when his guest arrives.” Having said all this in one breath, Zuo suddenly called, “Xueyan!” “What are your instructions, Your Excellency?” “Is Focke in Shanghai?” “Yes. He was about to return home, but on hearing of your inspection he specially postponed his departure by one steamer. He will certainly call on you tomorrow.” “Will he come back after returning to Germany?” “Yes, indeed.” “Good. Then we can discuss the matter further and take advantage of his journey home to have him purchase any new and effective weapons.”

zh: 胡雪岩正待回答，只见一名戈什哈掀帘而入，手里持着一个卷夹，走到左宗棠面前，一言不发，只将卷夹打了开来，里面张纸；左宗棠拿起来看完，随手便递了给胡雪岩。接过来一看，是一份密电的译文∶『申局探呈左爵相，（享密）沅帅督粤，即明发。』署名是一个『云』字，胡雪岩知道，是徐用仪发来的密电。这『沅帅』当然是指号沅甫的曾国荃，胡雪岩笑道∶『两广是好地方。曾九帅这回不会象去年那样，陕甘总督当不到半年，就因为太苦而一定要求去了。』左宗棠点点头，沉吟了一会，抬起头来，徐徐说道∶『叫曾老九到两广，可见张振仙是不会回任，要真除直督了。雪岩，我要乘此机会，大加整顿，南洋的归南洋，北洋的归北洋，把李少荃那只看不见的「三只手」消除出去。』『是。』胡雪岩心想李鸿章在南洋的势力，已有根深柢固之势，要清除不容易；但真的办到了，将来另有一番局面，这件事值得出一番大气力。
en: Hu was about to reply when a personal guard lifted the curtain and entered with a document folder. Without speaking, he approached Zuo and opened it. There was a sheet inside. Zuo read it and immediately passed it to Hu. It was the decoded text of a confidential telegram: “Shanghai office respectfully reports to Marquis Zuo: [confidential] Marshal Yuan to govern Liangguang; public appointment decree imminent.” The signature was the single character “Yun.” Hu knew the message came from Xu Yongyi. Marshal Yuan was, of course, Zeng Guoquan, whose courtesy name was Yuanfu. Hu smiled. “Liangguang is a good place. This time Ninth Marshal Zeng will not be like last year, when he insisted on leaving the governorship-general of Shaanxi and Gansu after less than six months because conditions were too harsh.” Zuo nodded and considered for a while. Raising his head, he said slowly, “Sending Zeng the Ninth to Liangguang shows that Zhang Zhenxian will not return there. He is to be confirmed in Zhili. Xueyan, I must use this opportunity for a thorough reorganization. Let Nanyang belong to Nanyang and Beiyang to Beiyang. We must remove Li Shaoquan’s invisible meddling hand.” “Yes, Your Excellency.” Hu reflected that Li’s influence in Nanyang was deeply rooted and would not be easy to eliminate. If it could be done, however, an entirely new situation would open before them. It was worth a great effort.

zh: 『明天我去看制造局，你最好跟我一起去，看看有什么可以改良的地方。』『是。我明天一早来伺候。』辞出行辕，不过九点多钟，十里洋场正是热闹的时候；上车时，古应春的车案悄悄说道∶『老爷，七小姐那里的约会是今天。』『你倒比我记得还清楚。』古应春说道∶『是不是七小姐特为关照，要你到时候提醒我。』那车案笑嘻嘻地不作声，只扬鞭驱车，往南而去。『七小姐是哪个？』胡雪岩问。
en: “I am going to inspect the arsenal tomorrow. You had better come with me and see what can be improved.” “Certainly. I shall attend you early tomorrow morning.” When they left the headquarters, it was only a little after nine, and Shanghai’s foreign settlement was at its liveliest. As they climbed into the carriage, Gu’s driver quietly said, “Master, your appointment with Seventh Miss is tonight.” “You remember it more clearly than I do. Did Seventh Miss specially ask you to remind me?” The driver merely grinned, cracked his whip, and drove south. “Who is Seventh Miss?” Hu asked.

zh: 『爱月楼老七。』古应春答说，『刚从苏州来的。』『人长得怎么样？』『不过大方而已。应酬工夫可是一等。』『看样子不止于应酬工夫。』胡雪岩笑道∶『扎客人的工夫也是一等。』『小爷叔看了就知道了。』转眼之间，马车在宝善街兆荣里停了下来，爱月楼老七家就在进弄堂右首第二家，相帮高喊一声∶『后厢房。』即时便有一名娘姨迎了出来。
en: “Seventh Miss Aiyuelou. She has just come from Suzhou.” “What does she look like?” “Presentable, that is all. But her skill in entertaining is first-rate.” “From the look of things, it is not only her entertaining that is first-rate.” Hu laughed. “She knows how to hold on to a client too.” “You will see for yourself, Uncle.” Soon the carriage stopped at Zhaorong Lane off Baoshan Street. Seventh Miss Aiyuelou’s establishment was the second house on the right. An attendant called, “Rear wing!” and a serving woman immediately came to receive them.

zh: 古胡二人便站在天进中等，只见那名娘姨插了满头红花，擦一脸白粉，丑而且怪，真是所谓鸠盘荼，但开出口来，那一口娇滴滴的吴侬软语，恰如十七八女郎，这就是苏州人所说的『隔壁西施』！『喔唷，古老爷，耐那哼故歇才来介？七小姐等是等得来。』及至发现胡雪岩，愈发大惊小怪，『喔唷唷唷，难末事体大格哉！啥叫财神老爷还清得来哉介？她这一喊不打紧，楼上纷纷开窗，探出好几张俊俏面庞，住天井中探望；其中有一个大声喊道∶』胡老爷，胡老爷，耐阿记得我介？奴是湘云老四，晏歇到倪搭来坐。『胡雪岩涉历花丛，阅人甚多，记不得有么一个湘云老四，只连声答应∶』好！好！『当下随着娘姨上楼，只见后厢房门口，有个花信年华的女子，打起门帘，含笑等待；等一进门，古应春说道∶『老七，你大概没有见过胡老爷？』
en: Hu and Gu waited in the courtyard. The woman’s hair was covered with red flowers, her face thick with white powder. Ugly and outlandish, she looked like a demoness. Yet when she spoke, her soft, delicate Wu dialect sounded like that of a girl of seventeen or eighteen: a true “beauty on the other side of the wall,” as Suzhou people called such women. “Oh, Mr Gu, why are you so late? Seventh Miss has been waiting and waiting!” On discovering Hu, she made a greater fuss still. “Oh, my goodness! What an occasion! How have we managed to invite the God of Wealth himself?” Her cries brought windows opening upstairs and several pretty faces peering down into the courtyard. One called loudly, “Mr Hu! Do you remember me? Fourth Miss Xiangyun! Come and sit with me later.” Hu had met so many women in his visits to the pleasure quarters that he could not remember this Fourth Miss Xiangyun. He merely answered, “Certainly! Certainly!” Following the serving woman upstairs, they found a woman of about twenty-four holding up the curtain at the rear room’s door, smiling as she waited. As they entered, Gu said, “Seventh Miss, I suppose you have never met Mr Hu?”

zh: 『啥叫见过歇？奴见过格。』说着敛衽见礼，口中说道∶『胡老爷，耐发福哉。』『喔，』胡雪岩问道∶『七小姐，我们在哪里见过？』『山塘畹？是大前年年脚边浪格事体哉。格日子是勒抚台格大少爷请客。胡老爷还转过奴一个局，耐末贵人多忘事，奴是一直记好勤心里浪向。』说着，便上前来替胡雪岩解钮扣，卸马褂。胡雪岩闻到她头发上的香味，记起有这么一回事，那年年底路过苏州，江苏巡抚勒方琦的长子，在上海便是稔友；特地在虎丘一家局书寓中请客，仿佛是在席间转过局，面貌依稀，但名字却记不起，但决不是三个字。『那时候你不叫爱月楼吧？』『伊个辰光叫惜芳。』
en: “Never met him? Of course I have.” She curtsied. “Mr Hu, you have grown more prosperous-looking.” “Oh? Where did we meet, Seventh Miss?” “At Shantang, near the end of the year before the year before last. Governor Le’s eldest son gave the dinner. You even called me over to entertain you. A great man has too much to remember, but I have always treasured it.” She came forward to undo Hu’s buttons and remove his riding jacket. The scent of her hair stirred his memory. Passing through Suzhou near the year’s end, he had been entertained by the eldest son of Le Fangqi, Governor of Jiangsu, whom he already knew well in Shanghai. The dinner had been given at a courtesan’s establishment at Tiger Hill. He vaguely remembered calling one of the women over during the banquet. Her face seemed familiar, but her name escaped him. It had certainly not consisted of three characters. “You were not called Aiyuelou then?” “I was called Xifang.”

zh: 『怪不得了。』胡雪碉笑笑寒喧∶『这几年还好吧？』『为仔好嘞，混到上海滩来格。』爱月楼老七向古应春瞟了一眼，『自从古老爷来捧仔场，慢慢叫好起来格哉。』『今朝日脚，勿壳张财神菩萨驾到，格末加二要好格哉畹！』插嘴的是那鸠盘荼，胡雪岩与古应春是听惯了这种奉承话，不以为意；倒是爱月楼老七听得刺耳，当即说道∶『耐闲话那哼介多介？』说着，又使个眼色，让她退了出去。这时果盘已经摆上来了，等胡雪岩与古应春坐了下来，爱月楼老七一面敬瓜子、敬茶，一面寒喧。『胡老爷是落里一日到格介？』『来是来了两三天了。』古应春代为回答∶『不过今天头一回出来吃花酒。』
en: “That explains it.” Hu smiled and asked politely, “Have the last few years treated you well?” “I came to Shanghai hoping for better things.” Aiyuelou glanced at Gu. “Since Mr Gu began supporting my establishment, things have gradually improved.” “And with the God of Wealth arriving so unexpectedly today, they will improve still more!” the serving woman put in. Hu and Gu were accustomed to such flattery and paid it little heed. Aiyuelou, however, found it grating. “Why do you talk so much?” she said, giving the woman a look that sent her out. Fruit trays had now been set out. Once the men were seated, Aiyuelou offered melon seeds and tea and continued the courtesies. “When did Mr Hu arrive?” “Two or three days ago,” Gu answered for him. “But this is his first evening out at a courtesan’s dinner.”

zh: 『啊唷！头一转就到奴搭，格是看得起奴畹！多谢、多谢。』『早知道你们是老相好，我昨天就请我们小爷叔来了。』『那哼叫小爷叔？古老爷，耐姓半个胡畹，啥叫是叔侄辈子？』『妙！』胡雪岩笑道∶『应春，我还是头一回听说，你姓半个胡。』古应春也笑了，回顾一班小大姐说∶『你们以后就叫我半胡老爷好了。』『格就呒趣哉！』爱月楼老七接口说道∶『吃酒末吃半壶，碰麻雀末一和还勿和。阿要作孽？』
en: “Oh! And you came to me on your very first outing! What an honor. Thank you!” “Had I known you were old friends, I should have brought our Little Uncle yesterday.” “Why Little Uncle? Your surname Gu is only half of Hu. How can you be uncle and nephew?” “Excellent!” Hu laughed. “Yingchun, this is the first time I have heard that your surname is half a Hu.” Gu laughed too. Turning to the young attendants, he said, “You may all call me Mr Half-Hu from now on.” “That would be no fun!” Aiyuelou replied. “Half a pot of wine to drink, and not even one complete winning hand at mahjong! Would that not be a miserable fate?”

zh: 胡雪岩看她心思灵活、口齿便给，颇有好感；古应春看出他的心思，便即说道∶『小爷叔，今天这个客，你来请了吧？』胡雪岩跟他走马章台，已历多年，间或也有这种『让贤』之举；正在考虑是否接受此番美意时，爱月楼老七却开口了。『勿作兴格！古老爷，耐今朝格台酒那哼好赖？停吃得有兴末，翻台到前厢房，胡老爷耐看阿好？』『前厢房？』胡雪岩问，『是湘云老四那里。』既然人家都已画好道了，逢场作戏惯了的胡雪岩毫无异议，只问古应春∶『请哪些人？』
en: Hu liked her quick wit and ready tongue. Gu saw it and said, “Uncle, why do you not take over as host tonight?” They had visited the pleasure quarters together for many years, and Gu occasionally yielded his place in this way. Hu was considering whether to accept when Aiyuelou spoke. “That will not do! Mr Gu, how can you escape paying for tonight’s dinner? If everyone is enjoying himself afterward, we can move to the front room for another round. Would that suit you, Mr Hu?” “The front room? Fourth Miss Xiangyun’s?” Since she had already arranged their course, Hu, well accustomed to these social games, had no objection. He merely asked Gu, “Whom shall we invite?”

zh: 『小爷叔想看哪些人。』于是胡雪岩随口报了四、五个名字，都是青楼中善会凑趣的人物；古应春下笔如飞，写好了请柬，点一点主客一共七人，便即说道∶『我们来个八仙过海。』说着，又写一张请柬∶『飞请三马路长发栈，沙大爷印一心，惠临一叙。』赘上名字以后，另外又用小字注了一行∶『有贵客介见，千请勿却。』巧得很，偏偏就是这个特邀的客人，因病未能赴约。不过今雨不来旧雨来，有个胡雪岩与古应春都认识的兵部司官林茂先，外放福建的知府，路过上海也住在那家客栈，得知古应春请吃花酒；这是照例可以闯席的，逆旅无聊，便作了不速之客。
en: “Whom would you like to see?” Hu named four or five men known for making good company in the pleasure quarters. Gu’s brush flew as he wrote the invitations. Counting seven hosts and guests in all, he said, “Let us make Eight Immortals Crossing the Sea.” He wrote another invitation: “Urgently inviting Mr Sha Yixin, staying at Changfa Inn on Third Road, to join us.” After signing it, he added in smaller characters, “A distinguished guest awaits an introduction. Please do not decline.” By an odd chance, this specially invited man was prevented by illness from coming. An old acquaintance arrived instead. Lin Maoxian, whom both Hu and Gu knew, was a Ministry of War official newly appointed prefect in Fujian. Passing through Shanghai, he was staying at the same inn. On hearing that Gu was giving a courtesan’s dinner—an occasion one could customarily join without invitation—he relieved the tedium of travel by appearing unannounced.

zh: 『好极，好极！』古应春颇为欢迎，因为这林茂先也是很有趣的人，谈锋极健，肚子里掌故很多，声色场中宴饮，必得要有这样一个人，席面上才不会冷落。台面铺设好了，名为『双台』，其实仍是一张圆桌；爱月楼老七拿一方簇新的白洋布，裹着一把镶银象牙筷，走到古应春面前问道∶『客人可曾齐？』『还差一位。不过开席吧！』这时胡雪岩便发话了，因为勾栏虽非官场，但席次也讲身分地位；胡雪岩名正言顺是首座，他不等人家来请，抢着前面逊谢。『今天这个首座，林茂翁推都推不掉的——』『雪翁，雪翁！』『足下听我说完，如果不在道理上，你再驳我。』胡雪岩挥手拦住他说∶『第一，你是远客；第二，你有喜事；第三，除我跟应春以外，其余跟足下都是初会，理当客气。』话一完，大家都说道理很通，林茂先便拱拱手说道∶『有僭、有僭。』等爱月楼老七安了席，首先落座。
en: “Excellent! Excellent!” Gu welcomed him warmly. Lin was entertaining, a brilliant talker with a store of anecdotes. A dinner in the pleasure quarters needed such a man to keep it from falling flat. The banquet was laid. Though called a “double table,” it was still only one round table. Aiyuelou approached Gu with a bundle of silver-mounted ivory chopsticks wrapped in a fresh white cloth. “Are all the guests here?” “One is still missing, but let us begin.” Hu now spoke. Though a courtesan’s house was no government office, seating still reflected rank and standing. He was unquestionably entitled to the place of honor, but before anyone could invite him to it, he declined. “Mr Maoxian cannot possibly refuse the first seat tonight—” “Mr Xue, Mr Xue!” “Hear me out. If my reasons are unsound, you may refute them.” Hu raised a hand to stop him. “First, you have come from afar. Second, you have something to celebrate. Third, apart from Yingchun and myself, everyone here meets you for the first time and ought to show you courtesy.” All agreed that his reasoning was sound. Lin clasped his hands. “Then forgive my presumption.” Once Aiyuelou had arranged the places, he sat first.

zh: 次席当然胡雪岩，其余都是稔友，不分上下，只留了主位给古应春，等他一坐下，小大姐立即捧上一个黑木盘，内中笔砚以外，便是一叠局票。『茂翁，你叫哪位？』『这里我是外行，而且昨天刚到，今天是第一回来观光，请你举贤吧！』『叫湘云老四好了。』胡雪岩说，『我记得她那张嘴很能说，跟茂翁的谈锋倒相配。』古应春略想一想，写了下来，便又问道∶『小爷叔你自己呢？』胡雪岩的相识可是太多了，笑笑说道∶『你替我作主好了。』
en: Hu naturally took the second seat. The others were old friends and did not distinguish among their places, leaving only the host’s seat for Gu. As soon as he sat down, a young attendant brought a black wooden tray holding brush, inkstone, and a stack of summons cards for the courtesans. “Mr Maoxian, whom shall you call?” “I know nothing of the place. I arrived only yesterday, and this is my first visit. Recommend someone.” “Call Fourth Miss Xiangyun,” Hu suggested. “I remember she has a ready tongue. She would suit Mr Maoxian’s conversation.” Gu considered briefly, wrote the name, and asked, “And for you, Uncle?” Hu knew so many women that he merely smiled. “Choose for me.”

zh: 古应春点点头说∶『我替小爷叔叫两个，一个是好媛老九。一个是——』『不、不！我想起来。』胡雪岩说∶『另外一个叫娇凤老五。』『何必叫她呢？』古应春皱着眉说。『你不要管，我找她有事。』于是一一写好局票，发了出去；首先来的是近在前厢房的湘云老四，小足伶仃，扶着十三四岁的一个小大姐的肩膀，进门问道∶『落里一位是林老爷？』『喏、喏！』胡雪指着说道∶『就是这位京里来的林老爷，现任的知府大人。老四，我特为给你做这个媒』湘云老四因为胡雪岩没有叫她，心里老大不悦；现在才知道是有意把她推给别人，愈发生气∶『谢谢耐！』她说得极快，同时将一双杏儿眼往旁边一瞟，都看得出来，她是生气了。
en: Gu nodded. “I shall call two for you. Ninth Miss Haoyuan, and—” “No, wait. I remember. Let the other be Fifth Miss Jiaofeng.” “Why call her?” Gu frowned. “Never mind. I have something to discuss with her.” The summons cards were completed and sent out. First to arrive was Fourth Miss Xiangyun, close at hand in the front room. Moving on tiny bound feet, she leaned on the shoulder of a maid of thirteen or fourteen. “Which gentleman is Mr Lin?” she asked on entering. “Here!” Hu pointed. “This is Mr Lin from the capital, now an appointed prefect. Fourth Miss, I have specially arranged this introduction for you.” Xiangyun had already been displeased that Hu had not called her for himself. Discovering that he meant to hand her over to someone else made her angrier still. “Thank you!” she said rapidly, casting her almond-shaped eyes aside. Everyone could see that she was angry.

zh: 原来这也是胡雪岩待客的一番苦心。这林茂先在京中亦是一个嫖客，但喜欢逛『茶室』。因为『八大胡同』的『清吟小班』，犹如上海的『长三』，而『茶室』则相当于『幺二』，前者号称『卖嘴不卖身』，非花钱花到相当程度，不能为入幕之宾；后者则比较干脆，哪怕第一次『开盘子』，只要条件谈拢了，便可灭烛留髡。林茂先走马章台，喜欢图个痛快，这就是他常逛茶室的缘故。因为如此，他举荐湘云老四，因为她在长三中以『裤带松』出名。胡雪岩心想难得与林茂先客途相逢，要为他谋一夕之欢，所以作此安排；但湘云老四未必明白其中的委曲，索性向她说明了吧。打定主意，自以趁好媛、娇凤未来以前，速办为宜。因此，等湘云老四照例一一敬酒、交代门面话，绕圈子下来最后到次席的胡雪岩时，他便含笑问道∶『我转你一个局好不好？』
en: Hu had actually made the arrangement out of consideration for his guest. Lin patronized courtesans in Beijing but preferred the establishments called tea rooms. The small refined-singing houses of the Eight Great Alleys were like Shanghai’s changsan establishments, while tea rooms corresponded to the yao’er class. The former professed to sell conversation rather than sexual favors; a man had to spend a substantial amount before becoming an intimate guest. The latter were more direct. Even on his first visit, provided terms were agreed, he could have the candles extinguished and stay the night. Lin liked prompt gratification, which explained his preference for tea rooms. That was why Hu had recommended Xiangyun, notorious among the changsan courtesans for being accommodating in bed. Meeting Lin by chance on his travels was a rare pleasure, and Hu wanted to arrange an enjoyable night for him. Xiangyun might not understand his intention, so he had better explain. It should be done before Haoyuan and Jiaofeng arrived. After Xiangyun had made the usual round of toasts and polite remarks and finally reached Hu in the second seat, he smiled. “May I call you over for a private conversation?”

zh: 『随便耐！奴是啥人介？高兴来，招招手就来；不高兴来，一脚踢到仔东洋大海。』胡雪岩笑一笑，向林茂先说道∶『茂翁，对不起，老四跟我为了别人的事，有点误会，我转个局跟她有说清楚了，完璧归赵。如何？』
en: “As you please. What am I, after all? When you want me, one wave and I come. When you do not, you kick me away into the eastern ocean.” Hu smiled and turned to Lin. “Forgive me, Mr Maoxian. Fourth Miss and I have a misunderstanding over someone else’s affairs. Let me borrow her to clear it up, then return the jade intact to its rightful owner. Will that do?”
